papers.title: Agentic Abstention: Do Agents Know When to Stop Instead of Act?
papers.abstract: LLM agents are expected to act over multiple turns, using search, browsing interfaces, and terminal tools to complete user goals. Yet not every goal is well specified or achievable in the available environment. In this case, a reliable agent should recognize that further interaction is unlikely to help and abstain from additional tool calls.

papers.title: Beyond IID: How General Are Tabular Foundation Models, Really?
papers.abstract: Foundation models for predictive machine learning on tabular data have recently gained significant traction in academia and industry. Research communities are increasingly evaluating tabular foundation models on diverse datasets and tasks, yet benchmark software and evaluation protocols remain fragmented.

papers.title: One-Step Gradient Delay is Not a Barrier for Large-Scale Asynchronous Pipeline Parallel LLM Pretraining
papers.abstract: Modern large-scale LLM pretraining benefits from utilizing Pipeline Parallelism; however, synchronous implementations leave GPUs idle during pipeline bubbles, wasting computational resources. Asynchronous Pipeline Parallelism eliminates these bubbles, maximizing throughput at the cost of gradient staleness.

papers.title: One Model, Many Latencies: Universal Speech Enhancement for Diverse Real-Time Applications
papers.abstract: Different real-time speech applications impose distinct latency budgets, often requiring separately trained enhancement models for each scenario. This paper proposes a one-for-all, real-time universal speech enhancement model that provides explicit control over both algorithmic and computational latency.

papers.title: SWE-Together: Evaluating Coding Agents in Interactive User Sessions
papers.abstract: Most coding-agent benchmarks are static: an agent receives a complete task description up front and is judged only by its final code. Real coding assistance is interactive, with users clarifying goals, adding constraints, and correcting mistakes over multiple turns, requiring a new evaluation approach.

papers.title: SAM2Matting: Generalized Image and Video Matting
papers.abstract: Despite impressive advances in image matting, video matting remains challenging due to the inherent gap between high-level tracking, which requires frame-wise understanding, and low-level matting, which focuses on extremely fine-grained details. A tracker-to-matting framework is proposed to address this gap.

papers.title: How Good Can Linear Models Be for Time-Series Forecasting?
papers.abstract: Time-series forecasting research has been moving steadily toward larger architectures, from specialized transformers to general-purpose foundation models, assuming capacity unlocks accuracy. This work takes the opposite position: most of the gap can be closed at lower cost by tuning preprocessing rather than scaling models.

papers.title: Drop-Then-Recovery: How Redundant Are Vision-Language-Action Models?
papers.abstract: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models enable instruction-driven robotic manipulation, but they inherit oversized language backbones from pretrained VLMs whose capacity far exceeds what is needed for short robotic instructions. This work studies architectural redundancy in VLA models by using transformer block removal.

papers.title: LLM Program Optimization via Retrieval Augmented Search
papers.abstract: Recent work has demonstrated the potential of large language models for program optimization, a key challenge in programming languages. A blackbox adaptation method called Retrieval Augmented Search (RAS) performs beam search over candidate optimizations; at each step, it retrieves in-context examples from training data.

papers.title: RocketSmith: Agentic Additive Manufacturing of High-Powered Rockets
papers.abstract: RocketSmith is an agentic system which intelligently automates the DFAM process for the development of high powered rockets suitable for launch. The system utilizes a large language model to orchestrate the execution of software tools to validate design characteristics such as flight stability.

cc_updates.body: Introducing Claude Sonnet 5: now the default model in Claude Code, with a native 1M-token context window and promotional pricing of $2/$10 per Mtok through August 31. Update to version 2.1.197 for access.

Added support for organization default models — admins set it in the org console; it shows as Org default (or Role default) in /model when you haven't picked one yourself. Added readable default names for sessions at start. Added clickable file attachments in chat. Security: claude mcp list/get no longer spawn .mcp.json servers that a repo self-approved via a committed .claude/settings.json.

Added CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_MOUSE_CLICKS to disable mouse click/drag/hover in fullscreen mode while keeping wheel scroll. Fixed hook matchers with hyphenated identifiers accidentally substring-matching. Fixed voice dictation on macOS capturing silence in long-running sessions. Fixed voice dictation auto-submit never firing for Japanese, Chinese, Thai.
